title: Classify active process guard health as running
summary: Maintenance health now classifies expected active Process guard evidence as a running state instead of a missing required dependency.
reason: An in-progress pipeline run can legitimately produce ActiveJobs and related-process evidence. Rendering that expected state as missing/blocked made a healthy run look broken and painted the Maintenance health row red.
behavior_before: A running pipeline process caused the required Process guard health row to be reported as status missing, counted as required missing/blocking, and rendered as a blocked red Maintenance row.
behavior_after: A running pipeline process is reported as status running/operator_status active, rendered with the active/running table state, and excluded from required-missing counts while still preserving close-readiness guidance.
manual_validation: DesktopApp Runtime Python: refresh_summaries.py --paths touched files - passed
DesktopApp Runtime Python: unittest DesktopApp.tests.test_application_facade_local_api.LocalApiServerTests - failed unrelated Completed-view static export assertion
validate_changes.py --require-worktree-coverage - failed: 233 unrelated dirty file(s) not covered by any unreleased packet
rollback_plan: Revert app/maintenance/policy.py and apps/desktop/webview/static/assets/maintenanceView.js to the prior missing/blocked classification for non-ok Process guard rows, then rerun the focused Maintenance policy/static tests.
notes:
Classified expected active Process guard evidence as running/active instead of missing/blocked so an in-progress run no longer renders as red.
Did not restart the live backend for browser verification because a media pipeline run was active.
